title_en: Weihai Jingyuan Construction Co., Ltd. v. Weihai Fuli Enterprise Service Co., Ltd. and Weihai Shengfa Trading Co., Ltd. — dispute over overdue construction project payments
ruling_gist_en: Pursuant to Article 279 of the Contract Law of the PRC and Article 16 of the Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects, after completion of a construction project, the developer shall timely organize acceptance inspection of the project in accordance with the relevant construction acceptance regulations. Such acceptance is both the obligation and the right of the developer. If the contractor organizes acceptance inspection without the developer's consent and unilaterally goes through the completion acceptance procedures with the quality supervision department, this infringes upon the developer's right to acceptance inspection. Under such circumstances, the acceptance report and certificate of project excellence issued by the quality inspection department cannot have corresponding legal effect because they do not comply with statutory acceptance procedures.

full_text_en:
Weihai Jingyuan Construction Co., Ltd. v.
Weihai Welfare Enterprise Service Company, and Weihai
Shengfa Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over arrears of construction project payments

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 279 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 16 of the Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects, after completion of a construction project, the developer shall promptly organize project acceptance in accordance with relevant construction acceptance inspection regulations. Such acceptance is both the developer's obligation and the developer's right. If the contractor organizes project acceptance without the developer's consent and unilaterally goes through the completion acceptance procedures with the quality supervision department, this infringes upon the developer's right to project acceptance. In such circumstances, the acceptance report and project excellence certificate issued by the quality supervision department for the project, being inconsistent with statutory acceptance procedures, cannot produce corresponding legal effect.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 210

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellee at Second Instance): Weihai Jingyuan Construction Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 4 Xishan North Road, Weihai City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Xihai, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Ma Xiaojun, Attorney at Shandong Huatian Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellant at Second Instance): Weihai Welfare Enterprise Service Company, domiciled at No. 75 Sifang Road, Weihai City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Ni Yumin, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Huai Zhun, Attorney at Shandong Dongfang Weilai Law Firm.

Original Defendant: Weihai Shengfa Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 16 Tongyi Road, Weihai City, Shandong Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Xuefa, Manager of the Company.

In the case concerning a dispute over arrears of construction project payments between the applicant for retrial, Weihai Jingyuan Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingyuan Company), and the respondent, Weihai Welfare Enterprise Service Company (hereinafter referred to as Welfare Company), and the original defendant, Weihai Shengfa Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengfa Company), the Shandong High People's Court rendered the (2005) Lu Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 16 civil judgment on April 19, 2007, which has become legally effective. Dissatisfied with that judgment, Jingyuan Company applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 56-1 civil ruling on July 2, 2010, deciding to bring this case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and conducted an inquiry on March 22, 2011. Ma Xiaojun, agent ad litem of Jingyuan Company, and Huai Zhun, agent ad litem of Welfare Company, attended the inquiry. This case is now concluded.

On April 28, 2002, Jingyuan Company filed a lawsuit alleging: On October 15, 1998, Jingyuan Company entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract with the China Rehabilitation Research Center Weihai International Tourism Base (hereinafter referred to as Tourism Base), stipulating that Jingyuan Company would undertake the construction of the Quansheng Apartment Building developed by the Tourism Base. During the performance of the contract, Jingyuan Company commenced construction on October 5, 1998, as agreed, but the Tourism Base failed to pay the project funds on time and in full as stipulated in the contract, causing Jingyuan Company losses including idle labor and interest, totaling RMB 1,651,753.78. The project was completed on December 30, 1999, and was rated as reaching the excellent standard on June 8, 2000, by the Weihai Construction Project Quality Supervision and Management Station. On November 9, 2001, the Weihai Branch of Shandong Jiangde Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. audited and verified the project settlement value at RMB 7,638,124.44, which was recognized by both Jingyuan Company and the Tourism Base. However, the Tourism Base did not pay the project funds, with an outstanding balance of RMB 5,767,123.8. In September 2000, the Tourism Base was revoked of its business license by the Weihai High-tech Development Zone Administration for Industry and Commerce for failing to undergo annual inspection, and all its creditor's rights and debts were handled by its founding unit, Welfare Company. The project undertaken by Jingyuan Company was a joint development project between the Tourism Base and Weihai Economic and Technological Development Zone Quansheng Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as Quansheng Company). In September 2000, Quansheng Company was revoked of its business license by the industry and commerce department for failing to undergo annual inspection, and all its creditor's rights and debts were taken over by Shengfa Company. Jingyuan Company requested the court to order Welfare Company and Shengfa Company to: 1. pay the outstanding project funds of RMB 5,767,123.8; 2. pay an excellence award of RMB 382,000; and 3. pay the losses of RMB 1,651,753.78 caused by Welfare Company's breach of contract.

Welfare Company filed a counterclaim, stating: On October 15, 1998, the Tourism Base and Jingyuan Company entered into a Construction Project Construction Contract. According to the contract, Jingyuan Company was required to submit complete completion documents and a completion acceptance report to the Tourism Base before May 30, 1999, but Jingyuan Company has not yet delivered them. Furthermore, the contracted project has not passed acceptance because it has not yet met the conditions for completion acceptance, resulting in the Tourism Base failing to deliver the houses to Shengfa Company as agreed, and being ordered by the people's court to pay Shengfa Company liquidated damages for breach of contract in the amount of RMB 1,370,850 (calculated according to bank interest rates). Welfare Company has already performed the above payment obligation in accordance with the effective judgment. Jingyuan Company's delay in completion caused other losses of RMB 1,270,000 to the Tourism Base. Welfare Company requested the court to order Jingyuan Company to: 1. provide as-built drawings and a full set of completion documents; and 2. compensate for losses of RMB 2,645,676 (as of July 30, 2002) caused by the delay in construction. The litigation costs were to be borne by Jingyuan Company.

Upon trial, the Weihai Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province (hereinafter referred to as Weihai Intermediate Court) found: On February 18, 1998, the Tourism Base and Quansheng Company entered into an Agreement on the Development of Quansheng Apartment Building Real Estate, stipulating that the Tourism Base would provide capital and Quansheng Company would provide the land for the joint development of the Quansheng Apartment Building. On the same day, the Tourism Base and Jingyuan Company orally reached a project construction contract for the Quansheng Apartment Building. Jingyuan Company commenced construction on October 5 of the same year. On October 15 of the same year, the Tourism Base and Jingyuan Company signed a supplementary Construction Project Construction Contract, stipulating that the area of the Quansheng Apartment Building project was 8,800 square meters; the scope of work included civil engineering, water supply and drainage, heating, and electrical installation; the estimated project budget price was RMB 4,400,000; the completion date was May 30, 1999; the required quality grade was excellent, with a reward of 5% of the project price for achieving the excellent standard; the Tourism Base was to provide three major materials; 25% of the total price was to be paid as a mobilization fee at the time of contract signing, 10% of the project funds were to be paid within three days of project commencement, and 10% of the project funds were to be paid upon completion of the foundation works; thereafter, progress payments were to be made according to progress, reaching 60% upon completion of the main structure, 90% upon project completion, and the balance to be paid after final settlement; if the Tourism Base failed to pay on time, it would compensate Jingyuan Company for losses calculated at the highest bank interest rate; if the Tourism Base failed to pay the project funds, Jingyuan Company could retain part or all of the project, with proper protection, and the Tourism Base would bear the protection costs and compensate for losses, including idle labor, caused to Jingyuan Company by the breach; when the project was ready for completion acceptance, Jingyuan Company would, in accordance with the relevant national regulations on project completion, provide the Tourism Base's representative with complete completion documents and a completion acceptance report, and the Tourism Base's representative would organize relevant departments for acceptance; if Jingyuan Company failed to complete within the agreed timeframe, it would pay liquidated damages, with the amount calculated based on actual occurrence; after approval of the completion report, Jingyuan Company would submit a settlement report to the Tourism Base's representative for final settlement.

After the contract was signed, Jingyuan Company continued construction. The Tourism Base paid RMB 200,000 on the date of signing; paid RMB 98,584 upon completion of the foundation works; paid RMB 638,670 upon completion of the main structure; by April 3, 2000, the Tourism Base had actually paid Jingyuan Company a total of RMB 1,870,986.7 in project funds and materials converted to monetary value.

Because the Tourism Base did not obtain a real estate development qualification grade certificate, when processing project procedures, it registered the "Developer" under Jingyuan Company's name. On November 5, 1998, and April 2, 1999, Jingyuan Company, acting both as the developer and the contractor, requested the Weihai Huancui District Building Survey and Design Institute to evaluate the foundation works and main structure of the Quansheng Apartment Building. The above-mentioned works were rated as qualified projects. On March 15, 2000, Quansheng Company and Jingyuan Company jointly issued a written notice to the Tourism Base stating that the Tourism Base's failure to provide funds in a timely manner had caused project delays, and requested the Tourism Base to raise funds as soon as possible, failing which the contract would be terminated. On April 5, 2000, the legal representatives of Jingyuan Company, the Tourism Base, and Quansheng Company all signed the notice. Thereafter, the Tourism Base ceased to pay project funds and materials. Upon application by Jingyuan Company, the Weihai Construction Project Quality and Cost Supervision and Management Station (hereinafter referred to as the Quality Supervision Station) issued a completion acceptance report for the project on April 30, 2000, and issued a project quality excellence grade certification on June 8, 2000, noting that the construction area of the project was 5,500 square meters. On June 18, 2000, Shengfa Company commissioned the Weihai Branch of Shandong Huide Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., together with Jingyuan Company, to conduct an audit and final settlement of the project. On November 9, 2001, the firm issued a Project Settlement Audit Report, determining the settlement value of the project in question to be RMB 7,638,124.3.

On September 18, 2000, both the Tourism Base and Quansheng Company were revoked of their business licenses by the industry and commerce department for failing to undergo annual inspection. The creditor's rights and debts of the Tourism Base were taken over by Welfare Company, and the creditor's rights and debts of Quansheng Company were taken over by Shengfa Company.

Separately, it was found that Welfare Company sued Shengfa Company regarding the joint development of the project in question. The Weihai Intermediate Court rendered the (2001) Wei Min Chu Zi No.1 civil judgment in the above case, finding that the main structure of the project should have been completed by April 2000, but as of November 20, 2001, the project had not yet undergone completion acceptance and did not meet the conditions for house delivery. Welfare Company was in breach and was ordered to pay Shengfa Company liquidated damages of RMB 1,370,850 for delayed delivery of the houses (which has been enforced). Relying on the above judgment, Welfare Company filed a counterclaim in this case, requesting Jingyuan Company to compensate for the losses of RMB 1,370,850 caused by the delayed delivery of the houses.

During the initial trial of this case by the Weihai Intermediate Court, Welfare Company applied for a new appraisal of the project cost, but within the time limit set by the court, it failed to pre-pay the appraisal fee.

The investigation record of Tang Xinjiang, the supervisor of the project in question, by the Weihai Huancui District People's Procuratorate on March 2003, indicated that the project in question was not completed when the Quality Supervision Station issued the acceptance report; the doors and windows of the project were subcontracted by Welfare Company to a third party.

During the retrial at the Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shandong High Court), Welfare Company applied for a new appraisal of the project cost. The Shandong High Court commissioned Shandong Zhengyuan Hexin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengyuan Accounting Firm) to conduct an appraisal of the building's project cost. On June 28, 2006, the firm issued the "Weihai Quansheng Apartment Building Project Cost Forensic Appraisal Report" [Lu Zhengxin Gong Zi (2006) No. 1011], concluding that the total project cost of the Quansheng Apartment Building was RMB 6,810,949.46, and the cost of doors and windows was RMB 348,426.85. After the parties cross-examined the conclusions, they reached an agreement on disputed issues. On August 10, 2006, they jointly commissioned the firm to issue the "Supplementary Explanation to the 'Weihai Quansheng Apartment Building Project Cost Forensic Appraisal Report'" [Lu Zhengxin Gong Zi (2006) No. 1011], stating: 1. On August 3, 2006, the Shandong High Court held a hearing on the project cost of the Weihai Quansheng Apartment Building involved in the dispute over arrears of construction project payments between Welfare Company, Jingyuan Company, and Shengfa Company. Regarding issues with significant disputes between the parties, through mediation by the court, the parties reached an agreement and reached consensus on issues such as roof insulation layer, roof waterproofing protective coating, etc., which involved changes to the original cost amount, which the parties had already acknowledged in court. 2. The project cost of the Quansheng Apartment Building increased by RMB 137,730.58 based on the original report.

During the second instance trial at the Shandong High Court, the court commissioned the Weihai Intermediate Court to investigate with the Quality Supervision Station whether the construction project in question was fully acceptance. The station certified that the project in question was fully acceptance, not partial acceptance.

When the Weihai Intermediate Court auctioned the building in question, it commissioned the Weihai Price Certification Center to conduct a price appraisal of the Quansheng Apartment Complex Building. On June 18, 2003, the center issued the "Shandong Province Involved Asset Price Appraisal Report" stating that the complex building was an unfinished project, with incomplete supporting facilities for water, electricity, heating, etc.

On September 16, 2002, the Weihai Intermediate Court rendered the (2002) Wei Min Yi Chu Zi No.10 civil judgment, ordering Welfare Company to pay Jingyuan Company project funds of RMB 5,767,137.74, an excellence award of RMB 381,906.22, and various losses of RMB 1,427,199.6, totaling RMB 7,576,243.56; other claims of both parties were dismissed. Dissatisfied with the above judgment, Welfare Company appealed to the Shandong High Court. The Shandong High Court rendered the (2002) Lu Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 297 judgment, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Dissatisfied with the effective judgment, Welfare Company applied for retrial to the Shandong High Court. The Shandong High Court rendered the (2003) Lu Min Yi Jian Zi No. 77-2 civil ruling, vacating the (2002) Wei Min Yi Chu Zi No.10 civil judgment of the Weihai Intermediate Court and the (2002) Lu Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 297 civil judgment of the Shandong High Court, and remanded the case to the Weihai Intermediate Court for retrial.

Upon retrial, the Weihai Intermediate Court held that the Construction Project Construction Contract entered into between Jingyuan Company and the Tourism Base was legally valid. According to the contract, all project procedures were to be applied for by the Tourism Base. Since it did not have development qualifications, it registered the developer under Jingyuan Company's name, resulting in both the developer and the contractor being Jingyuan Company in the quality evaluation and acceptance reports for the project. This fact was recognized, and it was presumed that the Tourism Base was aware of the above fact, and the result was caused by the Tourism Base's conduct; Jingyuan Company should not bear responsibility. Because the Tourism Base failed to pay project funds on time, Quansheng Company and Jingyuan Company jointly issued a written notice of termination of the contract to it. The legal representative of the Tourism Base signed the notice. Thereafter, the Tourism Base ceased to pay project funds to Jingyuan Company. The above conduct of the Tourism Base was sufficient to give Jingyuan Company reasonable grounds to believe that the Tourism Base's signature on the notice of termination signified its agreement to terminate the contract. This statement prompted Jingyuan Company and Quansheng Company to conduct a final settlement of the project. Therefore, Jingyuan Company's failure to settle with Welfare Company, and its settlement with Shengfa Company, was deemed reasonable. Moreover, the appraisal was conducted by a qualified department in accordance with legal procedures, and the project completion acceptance report and project quality assessment certificate were issued, having legal force and should serve as the basis for deciding this case. Investigation confirmed that the project was fully acceptance, not partial acceptance. Therefore, Jingyuan Company's request for an order for Welfare Company to pay the project funds and interest, and to pay the excellence award, was well-founded and should be supported. The Tourism Base failed to pay project funds promptly as stipulated in the contract, and should bear the costs of protecting the project and compensate Jingyuan Company for losses due to idle equipment and revolving materials. Given that the cooperative development contract between the Tourism Base and Quansheng Company expressly stipulated that Quansheng Company would provide the land and the Tourism Base would provide the capital, and that the Construction Project Construction Contract in question was also signed between Jingyuan Company and the Tourism Base, Jingyuan Company's request for Shengfa Company to bear joint and several liability lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. Because the Tourism Base's insufficient investment caused the project to be delayed, Welfare Company's counterclaim was not well-founded and was not supported. The project in dispute was already a completed project; Welfare Company's counterclaim for losses for the uncompleted part of 5,000 square meters was not well-founded and was not supported.

On January 25, 2005, the Weihai Intermediate Court rendered the (2002) Wei Min Yi Zai Zhong Chu Zi No.10 civil judgment (hereinafter referred to as the first instance judgment of the Weihai Intermediate Court): (1) Welfare Company shall pay Jingyuan Company project funds of RMB 5,767,137.74; (2) Welfare Company shall pay Jingyuan Company an excellence award of RMB 381,906.22; (3) Welfare Company shall compensate Jingyuan Company for interest losses on the project funds of RMB 852,264.7, project storage costs of RMB 53,150, and losses due to idle equipment and revolving materials of RMB 521,784.9, totaling RMB 1,427,199.6; (4) dismiss Jingyuan Company's claim for Shengfa Company to bear joint and several payment obligations; (5) dismiss Welfare Company's claim for Jingyuan Company to compensate it for economic losses of RMB 264,576; (6) Jingyuan Company shall provide Welfare Company with as-built drawings and a completion acceptance report, one copy each.

Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment of the Weihai Intermediate Court, Welfare Company appealed to the Shandong High Court.

In its second instance trial, the Shandong High Court held that the key issues in this case were: 1. Whether the project in question was completed at the time of acceptance by the Quality Supervision Station; 2. Whether the completion acceptance report issued by the Quality Supervision Station was valid and whether the excellence award should be supported; 3. What was the project cost in question; 4. Whether the Tourism Base should pay liquidated damages for overdue payment; 5. Which party should bear the costs for project storage, losses due to idle equipment and revolving materials, and losses resulting from the delayed delivery of the project to Shengfa Company.

Regarding whether the project in question was completed: The (2001) Wei Min Chu Zi No.1 civil judgment of the Weihai Intermediate Court found that the project had not yet undergone completion acceptance as of November 20, 2001, and that judgment had become legally effective and should be used as valid evidence. Since the Quality Supervision Station conducted the completion acceptance in April 2000, this evidence showed that the project was not completed when the station issued the completion acceptance report and the excellence project evaluation certificate. The completion acceptance report and the excellence project evaluation certificate issued by the station were inconsistent with the facts. Furthermore, in accordance with the contract and relevant laws and regulations, the project in question should have been organized for acceptance by the developer, the Tourism Base. Jingyuan Company, as the contractor, unilaterally commissioned the Quality Supervision Station to conduct the acceptance, which violated the contract and relevant laws and regulations, and the procedure was illegal. Therefore, the acceptance report and the project evaluation certificate issued by the Quality Supervision Station should be deemed invalid. Jingyuan Company's claim for the excellence award of RMB 381,906.22 lacked factual basis and was not supported.

Regarding the project cost in question: According to the contract and relevant laws and regulations, after completion of the project in question, the contractor, Jingyuan Company, should have provided a settlement report to the developer, the Tourism Base, for the Tourism Base to approve the settlement. The settlement report issued by the Weihai Branch of Shandong Huide Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. was commissioned by Shengfa Company, which was not a party to the contract. The final settlement between Shengfa Company and Jingyuan Company for the project in question violated the contract and the law, rendering the settlement invalid and not usable as a basis for deciding the case. The judicial appraisal report and supplementary explanation issued by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm for the project in question were procedurally lawful, objective in content, and had been cross-examined by the parties; they were legally valid and should serve as the basis for deciding the case. The report determined the project value in question as RMB 6,948,680.04. After deducting the cost of doors and windows of RMB 348,426.85 and the project funds and materials valued at RMB 1,870,986.7 paid by the Tourism Company, the Tourism Base still owed Jingyuan Company project funds of RMB 4,729,266.49.

Regarding the issue of whether the Tourism Base should pay liquidated damages for overdue payment. The Tourism Base failed to disburse the project funds in a timely and full amount as stipulated in the contract, and according to the contract, it shall compensate for the losses of Jingyuan Company. As per the contract, such losses should be calculated segmentally based on the amounts due but unpaid by the Tourism Base and the time periods for which such amounts were overdue. The first instance determined that the calculation should be based on the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, and both parties raised no objection to this, so it should be adopted. After Jingyuan Company issued the notice of contract termination, and in the absence of any subsequent handling of the matter by the parties, Jingyuan Company, in its own name, commissioned an acceptance inspection of the unfinished project on April 30, 2000. Losses incurred thereafter should be borne by Jingyuan Company, while losses caused by the Tourism Base's failure to pay on time should be calculated up to April 30, 2000. Therefore, the losses caused to Jingyuan Company by the Tourism Base's delayed payment, calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, based on the overdue amounts and time periods as stipulated in the contract, shall be calculated up to April 30, 2000.

Regarding the issues of who should bear the costs of project storage, equipment and revolving material idle costs, and losses caused by delayed delivery of the project to Shengfa Company. The Quansheng Apartment Building was scheduled for completion on May 30, 1999, but was not completed. The storage costs due to the delay amounted to 53,450 yuan, and the idle costs for equipment and revolving materials amounted to 521,784.9 yuan. Welfare Company's delayed delivery of the project in question to Shengfa Company resulted in a judgment by Weihai Intermediate People's Court in Civil Judgment No. 1 (2001) Wei Min Chu Zi, ordering it to compensate Shengfa Company for actual economic losses (which have been fully enforced). These losses were caused by both the Tourism Base's failure to disburse funds adequately and Jingyuan Company's failure to complete the project as agreed. The Tourism Base's inadequate fund disbursement was the primary cause of the losses and shall bear primary responsibility; Jingyuan Company's failure to complete the project as agreed was a secondary cause and shall bear secondary responsibility. Based on the principle of fairness, 70% of the above losses shall be borne by the Tourism Base, and 30% by Jingyuan Company.

After the Tourism Base was dissolved, its claims and debts were succeeded by Welfare Company, so the above debts of the Tourism Base shall be repaid by Welfare Company.

The Shandong High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 16 (2005) Lu Min Zai Zhong Zi (hereinafter referred to as the Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court) on April 19, 2007: 1. Reversing Items 2, 3, and 5 of the First Instance Judgment of Weihai Intermediate Court; 2. Affirming Items 4 and 6 of the First Instance Judgment of Weihai Intermediate Court; 3. Amending Item 1 of the First Instance Judgment of Weihai Intermediate Court to: Welfare Company shall pay Jingyuan Company project funds of 4,729,266.49 yuan; 4. Welfare Company shall pay Jingyuan Company liquidated damages for overdue payment, calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, based on the overdue amounts that should have been but were not disbursed as per the contract, and calculated segmentally up to April 30, 2000, totaling 140,893 yuan; 5. Welfare Company shall pay Jingyuan Company 70% of the project storage costs, equipment and revolving material idle costs, totaling 402,664.43 yuan; 6. As for the 1,370,850 yuan Welfare Company compensated Shengfa Company due to the delayed delivery of the project in question, 30% thereof, i.e., 411,255 yuan, shall be borne by Jingyuan Company. For the above amounts, if payment is delayed, interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled.

Jingyuan Company, dissatisfied with the Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court, applied to this Court for retrial, requesting the reversal of the Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court and the affirmation of the First Instance Judgment of Weihai Intermediate Court. Main reasons:

1. The Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court adopted the appraisal report issued by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm, which was an erroneous application of law.

During the first instance trial in Weihai Intermediate Court, Welfare Company applied for a reappraisal of the project cost, but failed to pay the appraisal fee within the time limit set by the court, thereby waiving its right to request a reappraisal. The Shandong High Court's permission of Welfare Company's reappraisal application during the second instance was an erroneous application of law.

Jingyuan Company raised written objections to the judicial appraisal issued by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm and provided relevant evidence. The accounting firm agreed to seven of the objections raised by Jingyuan Company and promised to issue a written amendment opinion or reply. However, Jingyuan Company did not receive the supplementary explanation from Zhengyuan Accounting Firm, nor did it have the opportunity to present evidence regarding the supplementary explanation. The Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court, however, mentioned a "supplementary explanation" and used it as a basis for judgment, infringing upon Jingyuan Company's litigation rights, and substantively reducing the project cost by over 1 million yuan, thereby harming Jingyuan Company's interests.

2. The first instance judgment's holding that Jingyuan Company should bear 30% of the project storage costs, equipment and revolving material idle costs, and losses caused by the delayed delivery to Shengfa Company was erroneous.

The "Construction Project Construction Contract" signed by both parties stipulated that if Welfare Company failed to disburse project funds on time, Jingyuan Company had the right to suspend construction upon notice and claim overdue payment interest, liquidated damages, and losses from idle workers, etc. In this case, the project cost determined by the second instance judgment was 6.6 million yuan, while Welfare Company, including materials, had only disbursed 1.87 million yuan, seriously defaulting on progress payments. Despite multiple notices, it still failed to disburse, causing Jingyuan Company to be unable to proceed with construction, with personnel and equipment idled on site, resulting in significant economic losses. However, without any evidence, the second instance court stated that based on the principle of fairness, Jingyuan Company should bear 30% of the suspension losses and liability for breach of contract, which was an erroneous application of law.

3. The second instance judgment's findings on the cutoff date for Welfare Company's payment of liquidated damages and whether it should pay the project quality excellence award were factually erroneous.

According to Article 119 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "After one party to a contract breaches the contract, the other party shall take appropriate measures to prevent the escalation of losses; if the losses are escalated due to the failure to take appropriate measures, the party shall not claim compensation for the escalated losses." After the project construction was completed and Welfare Company agreed to terminate the contract and withdraw from the cooperative development, and in the absence of any further communication, Jingyuan Company, aiming to minimize all parties' losses, organized the completion acceptance inspection without fault. Moreover, when the Tourism Base handled the commencement procedures, it listed Jingyuan Company as the construction unit, so the project completion acceptance inspection could only be organized by Jingyuan Company as the applicant. Even if Jingyuan Company should not have organized the acceptance inspection, Welfare Company should have paid 2.64 million yuan in project funds before the main structure was completed, but it only paid 1.87 million yuan. This portion of overdue project funds persisted continuously and did not cease on April 30, 2000. The second instance court's finding that Jingyuan Company commissioned an acceptance inspection of the unfinished project in its own name on April 30, 2000, and that subsequent losses should be borne by Jingyuan Company, and that losses caused by the Tourism Base's failure to disburse on time should be calculated up to April 30, 2000, was erroneous.

Regarding whether the project was completed and accepted and whether the quality excellence award should be paid, the second instance judgment found: "Civil Judgment No. 1 (2001) Wei Min Chu Zi of Weihai Intermediate Court has become legally effective, and the facts found in that judgment shall be used as valid evidence." However, the finding on page 7 of the above judgment that the project was "not completed and accepted" was inconsistent with the fact found on page 4 that there was no comprehensive acceptance, which was clearly an inadvertent error. The second instance court interpreted the above judgment one-sidedly, resulting in an erroneous application of law. Moreover, according to relevant state regulations and the parties' contractual agreement, the quality supervision station is the administrative authority for project quality assessment. The completion acceptance certificate and construction project quality grade assessment certificate it issues cannot have their validity denied without legal procedures. Furthermore, Welfare Company itself stated in its complaint that the project was completed. Therefore, it is an indisputable fact that the Quansheng Apartment Building was completed in April 2000 and was of excellent quality. Jingyuan Company's claim for the quality excellence award of 381,906.22 yuan should be supported.

Welfare Company argued in its defense: (1) The main evidence supporting the facts found in the second instance judgment was challenged through cross-examination. 1. Welfare Company's application for reappraisal of the project in question was in accordance with the law. Article 28 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings" stipulates: "If one party entrusts a relevant department to make an expert conclusion on its own, and the other party has sufficient evidence to rebut it and applies for a reappraisal, the people's court shall permit it." On June 18, 2000, Shengfa Company commissioned Shandong Huide Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., Weihai Branch, and Jingyuan Company to conduct an audit and final settlement of the project in question. The firm issued an appraisal report stating that the settlement value of the project was 7,638,124.3 yuan. Shengfa Company was not a party to the contract, and its entrustment of others to settle the project with Jingyuan Company violated the contract and legal provisions; the settlement was invalid and could not be used as the basis for judgment. In 2005, after learning that Tang Xinjian, a supervisor from Weihai Construction Supervision Company, had provided testimony in the Weihai Huancui District People's Procuratorate that the project in question was unfinished, Welfare Company applied for a reappraisal of the project cost during the second trial of this case in the Shandong High Court. The Shandong High Court entrusted Shandong Zhengyuan Hexin Certified Public Accountants to conduct a judicial appraisal of the project value. Jingyuan Company agreed to this, and the judicial appraisal complied with legal provisions. 2. The judicial appraisal made by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm for the project in question was subject to cross-examination.

The judicial appraisal report and supplementary explanation issued by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm for the project in question were procedurally lawful, objective in content, and, having been challenged by the parties through cross-examination, were legally valid and should be used as the basis for judgment.

(2) The original trial judgment correctly applied the law. 1. Jingyuan Company, as the contractor, unilaterally conducted an acceptance inspection of the project, causing significant losses to Welfare Company, and should accordingly assume liability for breach of contract. Although the construction unit listed on the project commencement procedures was Jingyuan Company, this does not alter the contractual stipulation and construction fact that Jingyuan Company was the project contractor; Jingyuan Company cannot represent the developer in conducting project acceptance inspection. On April 5, 2000, the "Construction Project Construction Contract" in question was terminated. Jingyuan Company was no longer the construction unit for the project, yet on April 30, 2000, it illegally commissioned the quality supervision station to conduct an acceptance inspection of the project. The second instance judgment correctly held that after Jingyuan Company issued the notice of contract termination, it unilaterally conducted an acceptance inspection of the unfinished project in its own name, and subsequent losses should be borne by Jingyuan Company. 2. Jingyuan Company's claim for liquidated damages for seven years is unfounded. After the "Construction Project Construction Contract" was terminated, the project in question remained under Jingyuan Company's control. On March 29, 2003, based on the then-effective (but now reversed) Civil Judgment No. 297 (2002) Lu Min Yi Zhong Zi of the Shandong High Court, Jingyuan Company applied to Weihai Intermediate Court for enforcement. On July 16, 2003, Weihai Intermediate Court entrusted Weihai Real Estate Auction House to auction Welfare Company's 3,759.15-square-meter building. On August 7, 2003, Weihai Real Estate Auction House auctioned the building to Jingyuan Company for a total price of 3,360,000 yuan, at a unit price of 893.82 yuan per square meter. On October 15, 2003, Weihai Intermediate Court's Civil Ruling No. 71 (2003) Wei Zhi Yi Zi transferred the ownership of the above 3,759.15-square-meter building to Jingyuan Company. Currently, Jingyuan Company's claim that Welfare Company should pay liquidated damages up to the present lacks legal basis. 3. The project in question is an unfinished project, and Jingyuan Company's request for payment of the project quality excellence award lacks factual basis. According to the facts already found by the court, it is sufficient to prove that the project in question is unfinished. Moreover, Civil Judgment No. 1 (2001) Wei Min Chu Zi of Weihai Intermediate Court, which has become legally effective, found on page 7 that the project in question was "not completed and accepted." On March 15, 2000, Shengfa Company and Jingyuan Company jointly issued a written notice to the Tourism Base stating that due to the Tourism Base's failure to provide funds in a timely manner, the project was delayed, requesting prompt fund raising; otherwise, they would terminate the contract. This proves that as of April 5, 2000, the project in question had not been completed, and the "Construction Project Construction Contract" had already been terminated. The contract stipulated a building area of 8,800 square meters, but the acceptance report issued by the quality supervision station indicated a building area of 5,500 square meters, proving the project was unfinished. On February 24, 2003, the Weihai Economic and Technological Development Zone Notary Office issued a notarial certificate (No. 78 (2003) Wei Kai Zheng Jing Zi) proving the project was unfinished. Staff member Tang Xinjian from the quality supervision station gave testimony before the Procuratorate proving the project was unfinished. The "Shandong Province Asset Valuation Opinion on the Litigated Assets" concluded the project was unfinished. Jingyuan Company's legal representative, Wang Xihai, also gave statements proving the project was unfinished.

(3) Jingyuan Company acknowledged that the First Instance Judgment of Weihai Intermediate Court and the Second Instance Judgment of Shandong High Court were legally valid and had applied for enforcement, indicating that it had waived its right to apply for retrial. On June 26, 2007, Jingyuan Company submitted an "Application for Resumption of Enforcement" to Weihai Intermediate Court, requesting the resumption of enforcement of Case No. 71 (2003) Wei Zhi Yi Zi. This indicates that Jingyuan Company accepted the second instance judgment.

The facts found by this Court are the same as those found by the Weihai Intermediate Court in the first instance.

This Court holds that the focal issues in dispute between the parties in this retrial are: 1. Whether the Shandong High Court's permission of Welfare Company's appraisal application and the entrustment of an appraisal unit for the purpose of appraisal in the second instance was a correct application of law, and whether the appraisal report can be admitted as evidence; 2. Whether the project in question was of excellent quality, and whether Welfare Company should pay the project quality excellence award as stipulated in the contract; 3. Whether the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court correctly determined the cutoff date for calculating Welfare Company's liquidated damages; 4. Whether the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court's holding that Jingyuan Company and Welfare Company should share the project delay losses in a 3:7 ratio was correct.

(1) Regarding whether the Shandong High Court's permission of Welfare Company's appraisal application and the entrustment of an appraisal unit for appraisal in the second instance was a correct application of law, and whether the appraisal report can be admitted as evidence.

In this case, the basis for Jingyuan Company's claim for the amount of project funds owed by Welfare Company was the "Project Settlement Audit Report" issued by Shandong Huide Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., Weihai Branch. This report was commissioned by Shengfa Company, which was not a party to the "Construction Project Construction Contract" in question, and its entrustment of the settlement was also not recognized by the parties to the contract. Moreover, the audit basis for the above report was the project settlement statement unilaterally provided by Jingyuan Company, which was also not recognized by the developer, Tourism Base. During the second instance in the Shandong High Court, Welfare Company provided investigation records from the Weihai Huancui District People's Procuratorate, in which the project supervisor involved testified that when the quality supervision station inspected the project, it was still unfinished. However, the above settlement audit report and the settlement statement provided by Jingyuan Company were both based on the premise that the project was completed. Based on the above facts, it can be determined that the "Project Settlement Audit Report" issued by Shandong Huide Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., Weihai Branch, was inaccurate in its audit of the project fund settlement amount and cannot be admitted as evidence. Considering the above circumstances, the second instance court's permission of Welfare Company's reappraisal application was not an erroneous application of law. Jingyuan Company's argument that the second instance court's permission of Welfare Company's reappraisal application was an erroneous application of law is not supported by this Court.

The "Judicial Appraisal Report on the Construction Cost of Weihai Quansheng Apartment Building" issued by Zhengyuan Accounting Firm was conducted by appraisers with the corresponding appraisal qualifications. The second instance court organized the appraisers and both parties to conduct cross-examination of the appraisal report, and determined in court whether the objections raised by both parties to the appraisal report were valid. Based on the court's determination, the appraisal unit revised the appraisal report and issued a "Supplementary Explanation to the Judicial Appraisal Report on the Construction Cost of Weihai Quansheng Apartment Building." Jingyuan Company claims that the appraisal unit did not respond to the objections it raised regarding the appraisal report and that the supplementary appraisal report was not subject to cross-examination. This is inconsistent with the facts found in this case. Jingyuan Company's argument that the above appraisal report cannot be admitted as evidence is not supported by this Court.

(2) Regarding whether the project in question was of excellent quality and whether Welfare Company should pay the project quality excellence award as stipulated in the contract.

Article 269 of the Contract Law stipulates: "A construction project contract is a contract under which the contractor undertakes the construction of the project and the developer pays the price." Article 279 stipulates: "Upon completion of a construction project, the developer shall conduct acceptance inspection in a timely manner based on the construction drawings and specifications, and the construction acceptance norms and quality acceptance standards issued by the state. If the project passes the acceptance inspection, the developer shall pay the price as agreed and accept the construction project." Article 16 of the "Regulations on the Quality Management of Construction Projects" stipulates: "After receiving the completion report of a construction project, the developer shall organize relevant units such as the designer, contractor, and project supervisor to conduct a completion acceptance inspection." The above laws and regulations indicate that the completion acceptance inspection is both a right and an obligation of the developer. The developer's organization of the acceptance inspection of the construction project is a necessary procedure for the project to pass the completion acceptance. The facts found in this case show that because the Tourism Base did not have the relevant development and construction qualifications, it registered the construction unit for the project in question as Jingyuan Company. Jingyuan Company should act in good faith and safeguard the exercise of the Tourism Base's rights and obligations as the developer. The "Construction Project Construction Contract" signed by both parties stipulated the time for Jingyuan Company to provide completion documents and acceptance reports, indicating that the Tourism Base did not entrust Jingyuan Company with its right to organize the project acceptance inspection. Without the consent of the Tourism Base, Jingyuan Company unilaterally handled the completion acceptance procedures with the quality supervision station and applied for a quality grade assessment, infringing upon Welfare Company's rights as the developer of the project. As a result, the project completion acceptance report and project quality excellence certificate issued by the quality supervision station for the project in question did not comply with legal procedures and could not have the corresponding legal effect. Jingyuan Company's argument that, based on the project completion acceptance report and project quality excellence certificate issued by the quality supervision station, the project had been completed and accepted and was of excellent quality, and that Welfare Company should pay the project quality excellence award, is unfounded and is not supported by this Court.

(3) Regarding whether the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court correctly determined the cutoff date for calculating Welfare Company's liquidated damages.

The trial transcript of the second instance in the Shandong High Court records that Jingyuan Company stated that the liquidated damages should be calculated up to April 30, 2000. The above statement should be regarded as Jingyuan Company's admission regarding the cutoff date for calculating liquidated damages. Its current argument that the liquidated damages should be calculated up to the date of actual payment is inconsistent with its own admission and is not supported by this Court.

(4) Whether the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court's holding that Jingyuan Company and Welfare Company should share the project delay losses in a 3:7 ratio is correct.

The facts found in this case show that when the construction project in question did not meet the conditions for completion acceptance, Jingyuan Company unilaterally applied for completion acceptance, infringing upon the Tourism Base's rights as the project developer, and also contributed to the project's failure to be completed in a timely manner. Based on Jingyuan Company's fault as described above, the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court held that Jingyuan Company should bear 30% compensation liability for losses caused by the project delay, which is consistent with the actual circumstances of this case. Jingyuan Company's claim that it had no fault and should not bear compensation liability is not supported by this Court.

In summary, the second instance judgment of Shandong High Court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The judgment of the Shandong High People's Court (2005) Lu Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 16 is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
